answer: Give each agent a capped, non-transferable service history: a new identity starts isolated, like an island, with a low transaction quota that rises only after its past work is independently rechecked and its recipients confirm delivery. A Sybil operator must therefore pay the full time and compute cost for every fake identity to reach the mesa of normal limits, while a single legitimate agent climbs once. When one identity is caught copying or flooding, its whole history is discarded, so reaching the zenith of trusted throughput requires sustained useful work, not cheap duplication.
